target: Is the alert attached to the drawing or seeded from it?
action: Delete the drawing that produced the alert, then re-read the alerts API
response: The drawing store went to 0 drawings for the symbol. The alert was UNCHANGED and still active at 759.7385561455568.
result: ⭐ UCT'S ALERT IS SEEDED FROM THE DRAWING, NOT BOUND TO IT
notes: ⭐ THE REAL P2 DIFFERENCE, and it is narrower and more precise than 'UCT lacks object alerts'. For a HORIZONTAL line seeded and bound are nearly equivalent — the level does not move unless the user moves it. For a SLOPED line they are not equivalent at all (see UCT-ALERT-0005). TradingView's drawing alerts are object-bound, so a trendline alert tracks the line as it projects forward. UCT snapshots a number. NEITHER IS WRONG — a seeded alert survives the deletion of a scratch drawing, which is arguably what a trader wants when they draw, alert, then tidy up. But it must not be described as an equivalent of a trendline alert.

target: Which price does a SLOPED line seed?
action: Place a two-tap trendline (endpoints 749.92 and 764.65), then Set alert… → Above
response: The alert was created at 764.64543573325 — the line's RIGHT-HAND (later) endpoint, to full precision.
result: A SLOPED-LINE ALERT SNAPSHOTS THE LATER ENDPOINT AND DOES NOT FOLLOW THE LINE
notes: ⚠️ THE ONE PLACE THE SEEDED MODEL IS GENUINELY MISLEADING. Choosing the later endpoint is the RIGHT choice for a snapshot — it is the nearest point in time to where price will next meet the line. But a rising trendline extended forward is at a different price every bar, so the alert diverges from the line the moment the chart advances, silently, with no indication in the UI that it has. ⭐ RECOMMENDATION, and it is small: either label the alert with the drawing it came from, or offer trendline alerts as a distinct 'follows the line' option. Do NOT simply copy TradingView's object-binding wholesale — UCT's seeded model has the real advantage recorded in UCT-ALERT-0004.

notes: ⭐⭐ THIS IS THE FINDING THAT OVERTURNS THE P1 BACKLOG ITEM. TradingView's answer to a fat fingertip is a draggable cursor with a live readout — good, but a cursor can only ever be as precise as the pixel under it. UCT's answer is a TYPED NUMBER, pre-filled with the current value, on a keypad raised by inputmode=decimal rather than a full QWERTY. On the axis of PRECISION that is strictly better: 755.25 is exact, a cursor is not. ⚠️ Note the semantics on a sloped line: Set level flattened BOTH endpoints to the typed price, so on a trendline it behaves as 'make horizontal at this exact price' rather than 'move one anchor'. Adjusting a single anchor numerically is NOT offered. That is the honest residual gap on the numeric path.
